problems.title: QUIZ 09 #5 — Satellite at altitude: period, speed, acceleration

md: A satellite is in a circular orbit around the Earth at an altitude of $2.58\times 10^{6}\ \text{m}$.
Find (a) the period in hours, (b) the speed in km/s, (c) the acceleration toward the center of the Earth.

wrong.hint: QUACK. Where is the center of the orbit? Measure r from there.
QUACK. Read the problem again. What does 'altitude' add to the picture?
QUACK. Is g still 9.80 up there? Ask Newton, not the sticky note.
QUACK. Check (a). What unit did your seconds turn into?

problems.title: HW 09 #15 — Period 132 min: altitude and g there

md: An artificial satellite circling the Earth completes each orbit in $132$ minutes.
(a) Find the altitude of the satellite. (b) What is the value of $g$ at the location of this satellite?

wrong.hint: QUACK. In $GM/r^2$, r is measured from where?
QUACK. 132 of what? Convert before you cube-root anything.
QUACK. Kepler hands you r. The question asks something else. What?
QUACK. Same g at every height? Then why does the Moon not fall in at 9.8?

problems.title: HW 09 #9 — Stuntman on a rope: tension at three points

md: A stuntman whose mass is $59\ \text{kg}$ swings from the end of a $4.3\ \text{m}$ long rope along the arc of a vertical circle. He starts from rest when the rope is horizontal.
Find the tension in the rope (a) at the beginning of his motion, (b) at a height of $1.5\ \text{m}$ above the bottom of the arc, (c) at the bottom of the arc. Give kN.

wrong.hint: QUACK. Sum the forces along the rope. Gravity has a vote there too.
QUACK. At the start, he is at rest and the rope is horizontal. Which force points along the rope there?
QUACK. Draw the rope at that height. Which trig function gives gravity's part ALONG the rope?
QUACK. At the bottom: how fast is he? Energy first, then the circle.

problems.title: QUIZ 09 #3 — Loop: release height and normal force difference

md: A roller-coaster track has a circular loop of radius $R$ in a vertical plane. A car of mass $m$ starts from rest at height $h$ above the bottom of the loop. No friction.
(a) The car barely makes it around (riders feel weightless at the top). Find $h$.
(b) For any release above that minimum, find $N_B - N_T$ (bottom minus top).

wrong.hint: QUACK. Where is the top of the loop measured from? Draw it.
QUACK. At the top, the car still moves. Where did that kinetic energy come from?
QUACK. The car is faster at the bottom than at the top. Did that make it into your difference?
QUACK. Write Newton at top and at bottom. Which way does $mg$ point in each, relative to center?

problems.title: HW 09 #1 — Swinging cord at 26°: tension and accelerations

md: One end of a cord is fixed and a small $0.400\ \text{kg}$ object swings on the other end in a vertical circle of radius $3.00\ \text{m}$. When $\theta = 26.0^\circ$ (cord from vertical), the speed is $6.00\ \text{m/s}$.
Find (a) the tension, (b) $a_r$ and $a_t$, (c) the total acceleration and its angle below the cord, (d) is the answer changed if the object swings down instead of up?

wrong.hint: QUACK. Does the formula care which way it moves, or only where it is and how fast?
QUACK. Radial direction: toward the center. Which way does gravity's radial part point at θ?
QUACK. Draw θ from the vertical. Which leg of the triangle is along the cord?
QUACK. 'Below the cord.' Measured from which line?
